display.purpose: The one big headline in the hero. Centred.

subhead.purpose: A second heading inside a section, next to its demo.

title.purpose: The name at the top of a card.

body.purpose: Paragraphs. Supporting lines inside cards and tiles step down to 0.9375rem or 0.875rem.

label.purpose: Pixel face, uppercase. IDs, dates, timers, counts, stage names, fact names and the sample label.

shadows.name: block-bevel-marigold
shadows.purpose: Lit top edge and shaded bottom edge on marigold blocks: primary button and selected stage.

shadows.name: block-bevel-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover state of a marigold block. The bottom edge shrinks as the block moves down 2px.

shadows.name: block-bevel-pressed
shadows.purpose: Pressed state of a marigold block. The block has moved down 4px.

shadows.name: block-bevel-green
shadows.purpose: Bevel for green blocks such as member tiles.

shadows.name: pixel-corners
shadows.purpose: Four hard edges that leave a missing pixel at each corner. Used on panels and cards, which need a 4px margin to make room.

shadows.name: quiet-outline
shadows.purpose: The 2px outline of the quiet button on Dusk Sky.

shadows.name: stage-socket
shadows.purpose: An unselected stage marker: a green frame inside, and a Night gap outside that cuts the dashed trail.

shadows.name: thin-outline
shadows.purpose: A 1px line drawn inside the edge. Used on neutral chips, fact tiles and the "+N" member tile.

shadows.name: warn-outline
shadows.purpose: The outline of a "look closer" chip.

shadows.name: check-outline
shadows.purpose: The outline of a fact tile that still needs a person to confirm it.

motion.name: step

motion.name: blink

motion.name: reduced-motion

narrative.overview:
Shortlist looks like a small world built out of blocks. A dusk-blue sky sits at the top of the page, and everything under it is deep meadow green. Buttons and markers are solid blocks with a light top edge and a dark bottom edge, so they look like something you can press.

The look is friendly, but the words stay plain. Labels say what things are: posting, board, tracker, deadline. The blocky style is in the shapes, colours and motion, never in the wording.

Nothing is rounded, blurred or faded. Colour areas are flat, corners are square, and things move in a few visible steps instead of gliding.
keyCharacteristics: Blocks have a lit top edge and a shaded bottom edge.
Panels and cards have stepped "pixel" corners.
A checker pattern (a "dither") joins one colour band to the next.
Ruler ticks run along the top of sections, with a short ID.
Marigold is the only warm colour.
Motion moves in steps and never eases.
Two typefaces: a warm grotesk for reading, a pixel face for IDs, dates, codes, timers and small labels.
A feature section is a heading plus a small working copy of the real app page.

rules.name: The One Warm Colour Rule
rules.body: Marigold is the only warm colour on a page. Use it for the main action, the current step, or something the user must notice. Never use it as a band background or for body text.

rules.name: The Flat Band Rule
rules.body: Every band is one flat colour. No gradients. To join two bands, use the dither strip (see Components).

rules.name: The Chip Colour Rule
rules.body: A chip's colour is its meaning. Filled green means the fact is in your favour. A marigold outline means look closer. A plain green outline is neutral. Never pick a chip colour for decoration.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: The pixel face is for IDs, dates, codes, timers and small labels. Sentences, big headings and button text are always in Familjen Grotesk.

rules.name: The Show It Rule
rules.body: A feature section is a heading plus a demo of the feature. It does not describe the feature in a paragraph. If the demo needs explaining, fix the demo.

rules.name: The Real Page Rule
rules.body: Every landing section is a small copy of a real app page, built from the same data and the same template helpers (small functions the app's own pages call to format a chip, a countdown or a fact). That way the landing page cannot drift from the app. Discover and Boards work this way today; the Tracker demo is still written by hand and should follow.

rules.name: The Hard Edge Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has zero blur. A shadow here is a drawn edge, not a glow.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: A pressed block moves down and loses its bottom edge: 2px on hover, 4px when pressed. The change happens in 3 steps over 120ms (`steps(3, end)`), not as a smooth slide.

dos: Do give pressable blocks a lit top edge and a shaded bottom edge.
Do use Marigold for one main action per view, the current step, and things the user must notice.
Do use the pixel face for IDs, dates, codes, timers and small labels.
Do join colour bands with the dither seam.
Do move things in steps (`120ms steps(3, end)`), and turn motion off when the user asks for reduced motion.
Do label demonstration content as sample data, with a sample label above the block.
Do show a feature with a small copy of its real app page, built from the same data and template helpers.
Do let a chip's colour carry its meaning: filled green, marigold outline or plain outline.
Do write labels in plain product words: posting, board, tracker, stage, deadline.
Do keep text contrast at WCAG 2.1 AA (at least 4.5:1 for normal text). White on Dusk Sky is 7.2:1.
donts: Don't use blurred shadows, glows or gradients.
Don't use smooth easing (`ease`, `ease-in-out`) on transitions or animations.
Don't add a second warm colour, and don't use Marigold as a band background or for body text.
Don't set sentences, big headings or button text in the pixel face.
Don't describe a feature in a paragraph under its section heading. Show the feature.
Don't hand-write a landing demo that the app's own data and helpers can build.
Don't use game words (party, quest, XP, levels) in copy, component names or section names.
Don't show where the team is: no coordinates, city names or campus names. A posting's own job location is product data and stays.
Don't copy colours or fonts from the older app pages into new work.
